verdict.rationale: Vercel documents on-demand server-side execution with Fluid compute, which "scales concurrency", and describes itself as a platform to "deploy and scale" apps. This is direct evidence of automatic scaling, but the pack never explicitly describes load-based autoscaling behavior or how large bursts are absorbed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of load-based autoscaling mechanics (instance scale-out triggers, burst/concurrency ceilings), documented handling of large traffic spikes, independent or hands-on corroboration of burst absorption.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can rely on load-based autoscaling to absorb large traffic bursts automatically

citations.quote: Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
Deploy and scale web applications, APIs, and AI workloads from a Git repository or the Vercel CLI.
Fluid compute allows a single function instance to handle multiple WebSocket connections.
